Perfect, the wall is not on campus. Take this bicycle. Don't marry it.
You came back with the bicycle and your teeth. You can borrow it.
Next week, buy your own. Or marry it. I said don't, but I can't stop you.

scenes.title: Mission 4: They have taken light
scenes.context: The power goes off. Everyone shouts "Ah, they have taken light!" like every night.

lines.text: You saw them. I can see it on your face. Tea is free tonight. Only tonight.

scenes.title: Mission 6: Mai Shayi knows
scenes.context: Mai Shayi Audu knows every rumour on campus and sells it with tea. He says the shades gather in the Sculpture Garden.

lines.text: Tea first. Then talk.
Shades? They like the statues. Statues don't run. Easy friends.
And the man in the coat. He comes at night. He doesn't buy tea. I forgive him anyway.
Never visit a stranger with empty hands. Even a ghost likes tea.
My tea. Fifty naira. Friendship is free. Tea is not.
He accepted the tea? Ehen. Then you're not a stranger any more. That's a promotion.
Go and sleep. Tomorrow, the court. Somebody there is collecting money from freshers.

scenes.title: Mission 11: Baba Dam
scenes.context: The pier is rotten in three places. Baba Dam, the old fisherman, can't fix it alone.

lines.text: You took something from my shore. I'm not angry. Now you owe the shore.
The pier has three bad planks. Somebody will fall in. Probably you.
Wood from the timber yard. Sand and cement from the civil workshop. Go.
Not like that. Like this. Gentle. Wood listens. Cement doesn't. Cement obeys.
I don't remember.
That's a lie. I'm old. Old men can lie once a day. That was today's.
Eat. Here. Fish. Don't ask him again. Not this year.

scenes.title: Mission 14: The dam at midnight
scenes.context: Baba Dam's nets come up torn every night, and something under the water hums when the lights go out. He wants to see it.

lines.text: You brought kilishi. Good. Throw it far. Then don't move.
Twenty years I've fished. I've never seen the water eat light.
Twenty years! Twenty years I've waited for this conversation!
It was guarding that thing. Not my nets. My nets were just in the way.
Take it to the electrical woman. Okonkwo. She'll know.
And tomorrow, come and fish with me. Only fish. No monsters.

scenes.title: Mission 16: Gather the crew
scenes.context: The Maker says the shades will gather at the Senate on the night of the next blackout, and that one person with a torch is a snack. Five people with torches is a problem for them.

lines.text: Batteries? Today? ₦2,000 a pair.
Yesterday the night was friendly. Today, prices follow the dark. Buy bread instead.
A businessman. ₦300 for you. One pair. Don't tell anybody my prices talk.

scenes.title: Mission 19: Up NEPA party
scenes.context: The light has stayed on for a whole week. DJ Kabiru says that deserves noise, and he needs a crowd, a snack table and somebody brave enough to dance first.

lines.text: For your face today? Chocolate is ₦300. For his face, ₦500.
Nothing. It is just expensive.

scenes.title: Mission 21: Express delivery
scenes.context: Emeka the okada rider has sprained his wrist on the busiest morning of the month. Four deliveries, his bike, your backpack, and his phone ringing the whole time.

lines.text: My wrist said no this morning. My customers did not say no.
Four drops. Take my okada. If it falls, you fall with it. Joke. Half joke.
For your face today, ₦2,000. It has pockets inside the pockets.
That one is free. Like advice.
Put it there. Don't shake it. It's the charging port. It's always the port.
Cliff? There's only the ridge above the Dam. Go. Before he calls again.
All four? Even the cliff? Hm. You can ride for me any day my wrist complains.

scenes.title: Mission 25: Paper trail
scenes.context: Mai Shayi has noticed a man in a good suit who visits the Bank after closing, every time the light goes. He would like to know why.

lines.text: A man in a suit. Bank, after closing. Every time they take light.
Banks close. Men go home. This one does not. I sell tea. You have legs.
Thirty years pouring. Never missed. Ask me about money, I miss. Tea, never.
Thirty years. Sit.
Torn pages. Hm. Somebody is not hiding money. Somebody is hiding a name.
Drink. Go and sleep. Names come out. They always come out. In time.

scenes.title: Mission 27: What the net caught
scenes.context: Something in the water at the Dam took Baba Dam's net and dragged it under. Tonight the net came back, and it is full of something that is not fish.

lines.text: The water hears. Tonight, the water is shouting.
My net went down at sunset. It came up at moonrise. Heavy. Come and see.
Things that go into the water at night don't go by themselves.
Leave her. She only wants her water back. Cut it. Slowly.
In the water there are things older than the school. Some of them are mothers.
The Maker away, the dark comes calling. Every time.
lines.tone: Audu: on his stall, as you pass

lines.text: Don't ask where he goes. Nobody knows. Even the dark doesn't know.

scenes.title: Mission 28: Wingman
scenes.context: Sadiq likes Joy, the radio intern. Sadiq has never said more than "Toh" to her.

lines.text: For a love matter? ₦400. For a friendship matter, ₦600. Love is discounted.

scenes.title: Mission 29: Night market
scenes.context: With the Maker gone four days and the market dark at night, a gang of older boys calling themselves "the levy" are going stall to stall, collecting a "light fee" for lamps that don't exist.

lines.text: For your face today, ₦800 a battery. The dark is expensive. I don't make the rules.
Then the rules are expensive.

scenes.title: Mission 31: The second eel
scenes.context: The thing in the water that pulled Baba Dam's net is a mother eel, very old and very large. Since the Maker's absence, the shades have been gathering on her, and she is lashing at

lines.text: She's angry. Not at us. At the dark sitting on her back.
Bring kilishi. She likes it. Don't ask how I know.
Not her! The shades! Light on the shades!
Not the big one!
She wasn't attacking the pier. She was guarding that. All this time.
She has a name. It's long. It's in a language the water speaks. Not me.
The water is not a cupboard. The water is a mother. Tell your somebody.
The water!

scenes.title: Mission 34: Everybody
scenes.context: The Maker has a generator, a dynamo and a coil that hums. He says that on convocation night, when the seniors graduate and the whole campus lights up, the dark will come for the light.

lines.text: She'll watch. I'll watch her watch. The water hears.
For everybody? For the school? …Cost price. Don't tell anyone. My reputation.
Chi-Tech owes me. Hajiya owes me. Chi-Tech owes Hajiya. Circle. Forty candles. Done.

scenes.title: Mission 36: Convocation night
scenes.context: Convocation night. The seniors graduate; every light on campus goes on at once; and Count Entropy, fully grown on a year of the school's fear, stands on the Senate steps.

lines.text: You know who gave that thing a cape? Us. First years. Long ago. We were scared.
So we drew it a face. It kept the face. Fear keeps whatever you give it.

scenes.title: Mission 39: New drip
scenes.context: Alhaji Needle will sew your first native. It will be ready Thursday.

lines.text: Stand straight. Not like a question mark. Good.
Bring three yards and a cap. Come back Thursday.
Wisdom is not measured in inches, young man. Stand still.
I said Thursday. I did not say which.

scenes.title: Mission 41: The mall never blinks
scenes.context: The whole campus goes dark at once. Across the road the mall is glowing like a ship.

lines.text: Batteries? For your face today, ₦900. Buy two. Trust me. Buy two.

scenes.title: Mission 42: Meter reader
scenes.context: Every evening, just before the campus goes dark, a Works van leaves the substation and drives to the mall. Follow it without being seen.

lines.text: Six evenings. Same white van. It leaves the fire station side, then light goes.
I sell tea. I don't follow vans. You have legs.

scenes.title: Mission 45: Shuttle strike
scenes.context: The shuttle drivers have parked over unpaid allowances. Phase 2 is four kilometres away and full of stranded students.

lines.text: My guy! Shuttle no dey. Today, keke is king.
₦150 per head. Don't cheat them. Don't let them cheat you.

scenes.title: Mission 60: Those who stayed
scenes.context: Count who is left: a tea seller, a nurse, a porter, a man with a coil, and you. No allowance is coming.

lines.text: Tea first. …There is nobody to talk about. Drink slowly.

scenes.title: Mission 83: Echo
scenes.context: Mai Shayi says you were rude to him last night. You were asleep last night.

lines.text: Last night you pushed my bench and laughed. No tea.
…You didn't? Hm. It laughed like you. But it did not greet. You always greet.

scenes.title: Mission 88: Fashion show
scenes.context: Alhaji Needle's collection on a runway through the mall. He needs a model who can walk and turn.

lines.text: You are famous now? Good. Famous people stand straight. Stand straight.

scenes.title: Mission 90: Touch grass
scenes.context: Baba Dam does not own a phone. He owns a boat and a great deal of patience.

lines.text: The water hears. So today we don't talk. Sit that side.
The eel has been restless. Something warm under the wall has woken. Not today's matter.

scenes.title: Mission 91: The real clip
scenes.context: Somebody's phone caught the real thing and fell in the fountain. Chi-Tech can save it for three favours.

lines.text: It's the charging port. It's always the charging port. Also it was under water.
I need rice (a bag, uncooked), a part from the MIB Store, and the owner's permission.

scenes.title: Mission 95: The eel's bargain
scenes.context: The fifth coil is in the spillway under the Dam wall. Baba Dam will row you.

lines.text: You fought it twice. Tonight you bring it supper. That is how debts are paid.

scenes.title: Mission 113: Three by road
scenes.context: The Garden, the Mall and Old Campus, relit in one run. Everyone you met in Year 1 holds the first.

lines.text: Tea first. Then— no. Fight first. Tea after.

scenes.title: Mission 120: Fresher
scenes.context: One last ride round all of it, with the credits rolling past lamps you put up. Then, some years later, a new student at the gate asks you the way to the Senate.

lines.text: My guy! Come back and visit! I'll be here! I own four kekes!

scenes.title: Around campus: bad driving
scenes.context: A car or bike has nearly hit you. You shout at the driver.

lines.text: Ah ah! Oga, look road!
You wan kill person?!
Driver, take am easy!
Haba!
Na so you dey drive?

scenes.title: Around campus: somebody hit you for no reason
scenes.context: You were walking past and a student hit you.

lines.text: Ah! What was that for?
lines.scene: Around campus: somebody hit you for no reason

lines.text: Ye! My body!
lines.scene: Around campus: somebody hit you for no reason

lines.text: Are you mad?
lines.scene: Around campus: somebody hit you for no reason

lines.text: Who sent you?
lines.scene: Around campus: somebody hit you for no reason

lines.text: Abeg! I don't want trouble!
lines.scene: Around campus: somebody hit you for no reason

lines.text: Leave me alone!
lines.scene: Around campus: somebody hit you for no reason

lines.text: Somebody help!
lines.scene: Around campus: somebody hit you for no reason

lines.text: I'm going, I'm going!
lines.scene: Around campus: somebody hit you for no reason

scenes.title: Around campus: bad driving
scenes.context: A car or bike has nearly hit you. You shout at the driver.

lines.text: Are you blind?! This is a school!
My leg! Driver, come down!
You no dey see road?!
Hey! Slow down!
Jesus! Careful!
This one wants to kill somebody.

scenes.title: Around campus: watching a fight
scenes.context: A fight has broken out near you.

lines.text: Ah ah! What is this?
Fight! Fight!
Somebody call security!
Leave him alone o!
This campus self.

scenes.title: Around campus: bumped in the walkway
scenes.context: The player has walked or run straight into you.

lines.text: Ah ah! Watch where you're going!
lines.scene: Around campus: bumped in the walkway

lines.text: Easy now!
lines.scene: Around campus: bumped in the walkway

lines.text: Haba, fresher!
lines.scene: Around campus: bumped in the walkway

lines.text: Sorry o!
lines.scene: Around campus: bumped in the walkway

lines.text: Take am easy!
lines.scene: Around campus: bumped in the walkway

scenes.title: Mission 38: Grand opening
scenes.context: The market is now a mall. Hajiya Ladi's goods are at the gate, her new shop is upstairs, and the only escalator goes up.

lines.text: You! You have shoulders. Come back, I will measure you.
Welcome! For your face today? Bread is ₦300.
That was yesterday's face.
You! Second year! Water? Cold? For your face today, ₦100. For his face, ₦200.
Nothing. It's just expensive. Supply and demand.
Good. First customer of the second year. I'll remember your face. And its price.
Because I'm watching the mall. Different thing. You'll see.

scenes.title: Mission 39: New drip
scenes.context: Alhaji Needle will sew your first native. It will be ready Thursday.

lines.text: Fila or kufi? The kufi suits a serious face. You don't have one. Take the fila.
Turn. Again. Hm. I am a genius. You are only the canvas.
Your father's size? No? Every boy wants his father's size eventually.
Arms out. Like a scarecrow. A confident scarecrow. Good.

scenes.title: Mission 40: Level two, round one
scenes.context: Basit holds every high score in the Game Room. He lets you pick the machine.

lines.text: Two drinks? For a battle? ₦600. Battle pricing.

scenes.title: Mission 41: The mall never blinks
scenes.context: The whole campus goes dark at once. Across the road the mall is glowing like a ship.

lines.text: Before the mall: light went and came like a tired man.
Now it goes at the same minute every night. Somebody is keeping time.
And your Maker has gone walking. When he walks, the dark gets bold.
It means I don't know the price of light anymore. Nobody does. Buy batteries.
Drink. Fear makes you thirsty. Courage makes you more thirsty.
That riddle man. Tanko. He says one true thing a year. That was this year's.

scenes.title: Mission 42: Meter reader
scenes.context: Every evening, just before the campus goes dark, a Works van leaves the substation and drives to the mall. Follow it without being seen.

lines.text: Somebody is not stealing light. Somebody is posting it.
Eat your bread. Tomorrow we find number one.
Fire station. Boulevard. Gate. Then behind the mall. Every night. Six minutes.
You go at five minutes. Don't be early. Early is how they see you.
Don't tell them it has a secret. Now they all want the secret.
For your face? Batteries are ₦900. For yours, ₦1,200.
Because you know why.
Prices tell stories. Read mine. Nobody reads mine.
Next week, when bread is ₦400, ask me again.
Correct. Bread is ₦300. Knowledge is extra.
And bring my cup back. The cup is also evidence.

scenes.title: Mission 44: Iron Mama hums
scenes.context: The Maker has listened to the ground for a year. He sends you where he cannot go: under the mall, after closing, to see what is making the hum.

lines.text: …To what?
…and my mother said I should have been a pilot—

scenes.title: Mission 45: Shuttle strike
scenes.context: The shuttle drivers have parked over unpaid allowances. Phase 2 is four kilometres away and full of stranded students.

lines.text: How much did you make? Don't tell me. Tell me. Okay don't.

scenes.title: Mission 49: Chief Megawatt
scenes.context: The mall's owner invites you up. He would like to sponsor your department.

lines.text: Someone in the Senate reads my prices. Good. Slowly, people are learning to read.
Bread was ₦300 when they started. ₦400 when they doubled it. Do the maths.

scenes.title: Mission 52: Phase 2 goes dark
scenes.context: While the feeder is argued over, Phase 2 has had no light for a week. Water, torches and charged phones go out in convoy on the long road at night.

lines.text: For your face tonight? Free. Don't get used to it.
Prices today: zero. Tomorrow: ₦500 more. Life is balance.

scenes.title: Mission 56: Light for everybody
scenes.context: The feeder must be switched back at three corners of campus, ninety seconds apart. Then a panel in the Senate asks what you saw, and reads your own choices back to you.

lines.text: Price of honest light: ₦250. Write it on your heart. Bread costs what it costs again.

scenes.title: Mission 57: Sign-out, small
scenes.context: Second-semester exams in steady light. Then the final-years sign out in white shirts, and you hold the markers.

lines.text: Long vac. You can't sit at home counting ceiling. Work somewhere.

scenes.title: Mission 60: Those who stayed
scenes.context: Count who is left: a tea seller, a nurse, a porter, a man with a coil, and you. No allowance is coming.

lines.text: Keke. Morning runs. I take thirty per cent, because I am fair.
Hold this screwdriver. Don't touch anything else. Congratulations, you're a technician.
₦20. Not for money. For company. You pay me with your sitting.
Garri is up. Everything else is down. Read that slowly. It tells you who stayed.
Diagnosis: it needed a slap. Like all of us. ₦300.
That one's not for repair. It's been here eleven years. Somebody's paying rent on it.
Envelope. Every year. No name. Don't touch it.

scenes.title: Mission 68: Night nurse
scenes.context: The Sick Bay generator is on its last cup. Fetch four jerrycans, driving as if eggs were in the back.

lines.text: My guy! Breakfast! I heard about the nurse. The whole road heard. Eat!

scenes.title: Mission 70: Called off
scenes.context: The strike is over. The buses come back all at once, and Kabiru has hidden a treasure hunt across campus to welcome everybody.

lines.text: She answers to oranges. Hold the reins softly.
Clue price, for your face: ₦100. Treasure hunts are commerce now.
She does that. She thinks winning is rude.

scenes.title: Mission 71: Bolaji's choice
scenes.context: The mall wants Bolaji skating in its adverts full-time. He has a withdrawal form half filled in.

lines.text: Full-time means full-time. Students have exams. Exams are not content.

scenes.title: Mission 72: Workshop nights
scenes.context: Group Light Work's project: solar lamps for the dark road to Phase 2. Dr.

lines.text: These batteries are tired but honest. Like me.

scenes.title: Mission 73: Test run
scenes.context: The first lamp goes up at dusk on the darkest bend. It comes on.

lines.text: I buy what they bring. Lamp, no lamp, copper is copper.
I knew the price. Prices don't say names. You have to walk to the name.
Since my wife died, I don't like the dark. I didn't think. Copper is copper.

scenes.title: Mission 79: IT letter
scenes.context: One letter, four stamps, three offices, two "come back tomorrow"s and a bank queue. Then a choice of where you train for six months.

lines.text: Prices are up because the mood is up. Something is coming. I can feel it in the paper.
It is a photocopy. ₦50. Or ₦45 if you smile.

scenes.title: Mission 80: First day at work
scenes.context: Your supervisor hands you a broom. Then a clipboard.

lines.text: Seven pens, ₦700. Or ₦500 for honest people. Are you honest?

scenes.title: Mission 81: Lucky goes viral
scenes.context: Somebody filmed your dance at The Floor and put a beat under it. By lunch the whole school has seen it, and a brand wants your feet.

lines.text: They are good shoes. I would say so even if I were not paid to.
We want your feet. Only your feet. In our slippers. Forever.

scenes.title: Mission 82: The collab
scenes.context: Lucky wants three stunts for one video: a wheelie down the boulevard, a wave from the Senate steps, a keke full of goats. Then you go to buy socks and forty people want a picture.

lines.text: I heard the goats were coming. A shop must listen.
The goats told me.

scenes.title: Mission 83: Echo
scenes.context: Mai Shayi says you were rude to him last night. You were asleep last night.

lines.text: He drank my tea and paid with a leaf. A leaf! Then he smiled like a photo.
Blink. Again. Okay, you are you. Tea, one hundred naira. Not a leaf.

scenes.title: Mission 85: Payday
scenes.context: Your first real allowance: ₦60,000. Home needs some.

lines.text: You survived Year Three on garri. That is a business qualification. ₦2,000 off.
Discipline is expensive. For other people.

scenes.title: Mission 88: Fashion show
scenes.context: Alhaji Needle's collection on a runway through the mall. He needs a model who can walk and turn.

lines.text: That is not mine. …It is good. I am angry that it is good.
Who is that girl? Hire her. Not as a model. As a fire extinguisher.
Ehn ehn. My fabric is crying. Again.
Dust. Harmattan. My eyes are allergic to genius.

scenes.title: Mission 90: Touch grass
scenes.context: Baba Dam does not own a phone. He owns a boat and a great deal of patience.

lines.text: When they shout your name, they don't know you. When they curse it, they still don't.
The fish doesn't know your name. See how peaceful.
Somebody brought a wet phone. Your face is in it. The REAL one. Come.
His sister. Ask him nothing.
Had. Has. The water knows. I only fish.
…Fish.
(later) …No fish.
The phone fishes for you. Let it go hungry today.
He used to sit where you sit. He said his sister fed the fish here.
Then one year, he stopped saying it. I didn't ask. Fish don't ask either.
I found it in the water years ago. Keep it. It wants to be looked at.
Not today. Let it go. It's only checking you have manners.
Salt, fire, quiet. Three ingredients.
He's back. The quiet one. The water sounds different when he's back.

scenes.title: Mission 91: The real clip
scenes.context: Somebody's phone caught the real thing and fell in the fountain. Chi-Tech can save it for three favours.

lines.text: Rice is a myth. I'll do it properly. Three favours: cable, screen, and a secret.
The cable is ₦1,500. The cable is also a warning. Don't ask what about.
Side effect. You're welcome. Your phone is a fan now.
Phone repair, ₦3,000. Emotional repair, priceless. Pay the ₦3,000.

scenes.title: Mission 93: Cook-off
scenes.context: The food court is half the price and the buka is half empty. She will not ask for help.

lines.text: I'm not spying. I'm tasting for market research. This egusi is a threat to capitalism.
I didn't win. I monetised the victory.

scenes.title: Mission 95: The eel's bargain
scenes.context: The fifth coil is in the spillway under the Dam wall. Baba Dam will row you.

lines.text: It will keep that one for you. Better than a padlock.
The eel decides. Not you. Not me. Sit straight. Respect is posture.
Not like a drum. Like a heartbeat. Like someone you miss.
It knows the Maker's boat. It thinks you are him. Don't correct it.
Now it has adopted you. Feed it on Fridays.
Now I have a dog that swims. Thanks to you.

scenes.title: Mission 98: Sadiq's surprise
scenes.context: You owe your roommate an apology for most of this year. Before you can give it, the whole room shouts "surprise".

lines.text: Today is free. Tomorrow prices go up. Something is coming again. I can feel it.

scenes.title: Mission 103: Sixth site (Heist 2: the Senate basement)
scenes.context: The sixth plaque says only "at the centre". One reference is in a room the library does not admit to having, four corners of campus have to be measured, and the centre turns out to be a room

lines.text: For your face today? Twenty naira. Eat now. Eat a lot. Trust me.
lines.scene: Mission 103: Sixth site (Heist 2: the Senate basement)

scenes.title: Mission 104: Megawatt's offer
scenes.context: The coil costs more than a keke. Raise it honestly, or let Chief Megawatt pay for all of it and put his name on the tower.

lines.text: When my prices went up for no reason, something was wrong. I never said. I priced it.
A shop must listen. A shopkeeper must not shout.

scenes.title: Mission 105: Parts from everywhere
scenes.context: Six people each have one thing the coil needs. Each asks one small thing in return.

lines.text: Copper strap from my first okada. Ride with me once round the ring, like before.
A float from my net, for the insulator. Mend one knot first.

scenes.title: Mission 109: The Chancellor's shadow
scenes.context: A letter on every board: "Convocation is cancelled." No signature. The paper is cold.

lines.text: I sell things. I hear things. A price is a sentence, if you read it right.
For your face today? Free. All of it. Go and finish.

scenes.title: Mission 113: Three by road
scenes.context: The Garden, the Mall and Old Campus, relit in one run. Everyone you met in Year 1 holds the first.

lines.text: Tea for defenders. Free. Today only. Don't spread it.
Free was yesterday. Today is business.
Normal prices. That means it's over. Or just beginning. I'm not a prophet.

scenes.title: Mission 114: Three by air and water
scenes.context: One pass over the tower beacon in a sky with no lights below. The eel lighting the spillway.

lines.text: The water hears. Tonight it also sees. Look.
lines.scene: Mission 114: Three by air and water

lines.text: It's Friday. You fed it. It remembers. Manners pay.
lines.scene: Mission 114: Three by air and water

scenes.title: Mission 115: Chancellor Null
scenes.context: On the roof: a blank figure in a gown. It does not attack.

lines.text: Second-hand evil gown. ₦500. I'm being generous.

scenes.title: Mission 117: Gown
scenes.context: A name on a board, a gown from the mall, and five photographs in five places with whoever mattered most there.

lines.text: Gowns. I sew them at cost. Don't tell people; they'll think I've gone soft.
It's ready. Today. Don't look at me like that.
A gown is like a story. Too short, people talk. Too long, people sleep.

scenes.title: Mission 119: Sign-out
scenes.context: A white shirt and a box of markers. What each friend writes depends on five years of what you did.

lines.text: Prices go up. Some things don't. Keep it.

scenes.title: Side mission 14: Emeka's keke
scenes.context: He has saved for two years. Go with him to buy it and stop him paying the first price.

lines.text: My guy, you saved me a whole month. I'll name it after you. No. After my mother.
Wedding? I'm not marrying the keke. I want to drive it.
She purrs. She actually purrs. I'm calling her Mercy. Because I needed it.

scenes.title: Side mission 15: Emeka's matric number
scenes.context: He kept his old ID card. Walk with him to ask a question he has been afraid to ask.

lines.text: Maybe tomorrow. …No. Today. Walk slowly.
I left in 200 level. My father was sick. Then he was better. I wasn't.
A form. All this time it was only a form.
What if they say I was never a student? What if my years were nothing?
…Come back. Okay. I'll keep driving until I can.

scenes.title: Side mission 19: AB and the water
scenes.context: He will not get in Baba Dam's boat. Sit on the pier with him until he does, or does not.

lines.text: One foot is a start. Two is fishing.
lines.scene: Side mission 19: AB and the water

scenes.title: Side mission 26: Mama Nkechi's recipe book
scenes.context: The book is falling apart. Chi-Tech can scan it.

lines.text: Done. Free. Family photos and family recipes are always free.
lines.scene: Side mission 26: Mama Nkechi's recipe book

lines.text: Saving it, Mama. Forever. In the cloud.
lines.scene: Side mission 26: Mama Nkechi's recipe book

scenes.title: Side mission 27: Mai Shayi's kettle
scenes.context: The kettle has a hole. Bright Electricals cannot help.

lines.text: Tea first. Then talk. …There is no tea. So there is no talk. Help me.
Tell him he still owes me tea from 1998.

scenes.title: Side mission 29: Baba Dam's net

Hold the suitcase properly. It has your whole life in it. And my good pot.

Six. In a ring. You see it? I've flown here ten years. I never looked down.
One bounce. That's a landing. Two bounces is a conversation. Well done.

The Maker's old coat inspired it. There is a name sewn inside his. Not his.
I didn't read it. Some stitches are private.

lines.text: Eat. People talk. Rice does not.

scenes.title: Mission 93: Cook-off
scenes.context: The food court is half the price and the buka is half empty. She will not ask for help.

lines.text: Stir like you mean it! That pot can hear doubt!
Dates first. Then water. Then my soup. In that order. Respect the order.
Help? I have been cooking since before your father had teeth. …Okay. Stir.
The bottom is the best part. A little burnt is party. Too much is funeral.
Three plates is victory. Ten plates is war. I don't want war.
My mother's egusi. Don't share it. Share the food, not the recipe.

scenes.title: Mission 95: The eel's bargain
scenes.context: The fifth coil is in the spillway under the Dam wall. Baba Dam will row you.

lines.text: My chest said you were on water. Are you on water? Get off the water.

scenes.title: Mission 104: Megawatt's offer
scenes.context: The coil costs more than a keke. Raise it honestly, or let Chief Megawatt pay for all of it and put his name on the tower.

lines.text: The store will match what the students raise. Don't tell my accountant. I'm the accountant.

scenes.title: Mission 105: Parts from everywhere
scenes.context: Six people each have one thing the coil needs. Each asks one small thing in return.

lines.text: The old beacon lens. Say the checklist. Aloud.
My biggest pot lid, for the top plate. Eat first. You're thin.
Brass weights from my scale. Last price: greet your mother for me.
Scrub the corners. The corners are where restaurants die.

scenes.title: Mission 107: Failure (the dream)
scenes.context: Your supervisor says start again. It is raining.

lines.text: Sit. You're wet. Sleep a little. Then I'll talk. Or you'll dream it. Same thing.
Now you've seen it, I don't have to tell it.
A pot of soup is not six cooks each making one spoon. Open the door.
You slept talking. You said "she feeds the fish". Who feeds the fish?

scenes.title: Mission 111: Project defence
scenes.context: The last test. Then you, a rebuilt coil under a cloth, and a panel that has failed better students.

lines.text: God is with you. God is with you. Also eat something.

scenes.title: Mission 114: Three by air and water
scenes.context: One pass over the tower beacon in a sky with no lights below. The eel lighting the spillway.

Is this your room? It's clean. Who cleaned it? Not you.
Come. Stand here. You look like you haven't eaten since Year One.

scenes.context: She has to give a five-minute talk. Be her audience six times in six places.

lines.text: (at the buka) Speak louder, my daughter. You're thin. And quiet. Both.

lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.text: The news said lights came back at your school with dancing. Were you dancing?
lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.text: Is it raining there? Wear something. Don't stand under trees. Have you eaten?
lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.text: Still no supper eaten. If you see a man in a lab coat, tell him to eat.
lines.tone: Asiya on the phone: on the phone, message

scenes.context: With the Maker gone four days and the market dark at night, a gang of older boys calling themselves "the levy" are going stall to stall, collecting a "light fee" for lamps that don't exist.

lines.tone: Uche on the phone: on the phone, message

lines.text: Your father says don't run so much. You'll finish your shoes. Have you eaten?
lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

scenes.context: The Maker has a generator, a dynamo and a coil that hums. He says that on convocation night, when the seniors graduate and the whole campus lights up, the dark will come for the light.

lines.text: He ate supper. Two plates. Whatever you're doing, keep doing it.
lines.tone: Asiya on the phone: on the phone, message

lines.text: I saw a video. Was that you? With the lightning? Have you eaten? Come home.
lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.text: Have you reached? Have you eaten? Who is that boy in the background?
lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.text: You are coming home? I have cooked. I cooked last week in case.
lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone

scenes.context: Count who is left: a tea seller, a nurse, a porter, a man with a coil, and you. No allowance is coming.

lines.text: Students have gone. Even the goats look bored.

scenes.context: She has colour-coded your week. Follow it for one day.

lines.text: Have you eaten? Who made you call? Thank her.

scenes.context: Carry a parcel from the mall to the forest edge. He is too proud to say who it is for.

My son studied here. He came home thin. So now nobody goes home thin.
Food don finish. That's what I say. It never finishes. Eat.

lines.text: There is a horse in my kitchen! Sit, horse! You're thin!

scenes.title: Side mission 62: KB's stockroom
scenes.context: Before m109, KB asks you to help him count stock, and leaves the price lists out on purpose.

lines.text: KB's prices? I always thought he was mad. He's mad and correct. Last price.
You drove through it on a bicycle. Don't start.
Hold the suitcase properly. It has your whole life in it. And my good pot.
Because you will want soup at night, and I will not be here.

You're the one from the Senate steps. Good. Fear and joy are both fuel.

Him. He's not coming.
Throttle. Straight. Wait. Wait. …Now. Nose up. Gently. You're flying.
Everything is small from up here. Except the things that matter.
That's not air traffic. There's no air traffic. There's us and a bird.
Look down. Count the bright spots.
Six. In a ring. You see it? I've flown here ten years. I never looked down.
One bounce. That's a landing. Two bounces is a conversation. Well done.
Did you just fly? Your sister says you flew. Come home. Now. Please.
lines.tone: Mum on the phone: on the phone, as you walk

lines.text: For my uncle. He won't eat if I watch. Don't watch either.
Everyone's somebody's something. Go.
You, sit. You're thin. Two papers? Two plates.
Then zero plates. …Sit. I'm joking. Sit.
Two days. He's never missed supper. Not once. Don't ask me where. I don't know.
If you find the answer, bring it here. With him.
Roses? For who? …Hm. Take the yellow. The red ones are too loud for Sadiq.
I tell them where they're going. Flowers like to know.
Every Friday I put the ones nobody bought on a bench. A special one.
Light fee. Light fee! For which light? There is no light. Last price: zero.
They come at nine. My traders are scared. I am not scared. I am annoyed.
Then go and find work for when there is light. Go.
You chased them and now you're carrying my onions? Who raised you?
Sit. Eat. You fought for my market. I feed whoever fights for my market.
That boy is a forklift. Who is his mother? I want to thank her.
Minute that I paid zero. Underline it.
One loop. No tricks. No heroics. Joy only. That's an order.
Take Bature. He's never flown. I want to see his face.
Are you seeing what I'm seeing? The garden. It's lit.
Every evening, from up here. Best sound in the world. Sorry. Carry on.
Harmattan. In my eye. Both eyes. Go.
Kilishi for an eel? …The best one, then. An eel deserves respect.
One loop at dusk, one at midnight. If the dark comes from the north, I'll radio.
Feed them? I'll feed them till they cry. You, sit. You're thin.
Eat before you save the world. You'll save it better.
My customer! You see what they have done to my market?
Carry these. Shop fourteen. No, one. They changed the numbers.

Checklist. Aloud. I want to hear every item.
My tomatoes! Are you people mad?

lines.text: Final broadcast for this lot. Play it loud. Play it slow.

scenes.title: Side mission 17: Joy's night show
scenes.context: The anonymous host has lost her voice. Read the dedications.

lines.text: You're locked in. …Who is locked in? Is that a student? Fine. Go.

scenes.title: Side mission 33: Kabiru off air
scenes.context: The studio mic is dead and he must MC a wedding in person. He is terrified.

lines.text: People will look at me. Radio people are not for looking at.
You're locked in! The couple is locked in! Forever! Station ident!
Good evening, Samaru Quarters! Hold your plates, here comes love!

scenes.title: Side mission 43: Sugar's accounts
scenes.context: She has an accounting test tomorrow and a full floor tonight. Run the decks for one set.

lines.text: On the one! …I have accounting at eight. Debit is on the left. I think.
(from a corner, with a textbook) On the one! …Debit, credit. On the one!

scenes.title: Greetings around campus
scenes.context: The player walks up and says hello.

lines.text: You are tuned to Samaru FM!
Request line is open.
No dead air on my watch.

scenes.title: Mission 1: Welcome, fresher
scenes.context: Registration day. You arrive with one bag, one admission letter and a mother's list of instructions.

lines.text: Good morning, freshers. The tall orange building is the Senate. Wave at it.
Today's weather: harmattan. Tomorrow's weather: also harmattan. Moisturise.

scenes.title: Mission 2: Belle first
scenes.context: Day one of real life: eat, go to class, survive, come home. Simple.

lines.text: First lecture? Sit in the middle. Front row gets questions. Back gets sleep.
KB says bread is ₦300 for happy people. Look sad, save fifty naira.

scenes.title: Mission 3: Two wheels
scenes.context: The campus is big and your legs are small. Emeka at the gate has a bicycle that needs a rider and a box of books that needs to reach the Library before Mrs.

lines.text: The fountain has claimed three cyclists this week. The fountain is winning.
Library hours: until Mrs. Shehu says shh. Which is any minute.

scenes.title: Mission 4: They have taken light
scenes.context: The power goes off. Everyone shouts "Ah, they have taken light!" like every night.

lines.text: Light has been taken. We are on battery. My voice is on battery. Speak softly.
If you see shadows moving in your corridor, it's your roommate. Probably.

scenes.title: Mission 5: The missing fuse
scenes.context: Dr. Okonkwo says the blackouts aren't Works Department laziness: a fuse is missing from the campus feeder.

lines.text: Shout-out to the two mechanics arguing by the workshop. We can hear you. Live.
It's Wednesday. If a girl with an umbrella says "see you Wednesday", believe her.

scenes.title: Mission 6: Mai Shayi knows
scenes.context: Mai Shayi Audu knows every rumour on campus and sells it with tea. He says the shades gather in the Sculpture Garden.

lines.text: Sculpture Garden at night? Bring a torch and a friend who isn't afraid. Two friends.
Somebody put a cap on the goat statue again. The goat looks better. Leave it.

scenes.title: Mission 7: Fresher tax
scenes.context: At the court, a big boy who calls himself "Big Sly" is charging freshers ₦500 to walk past it. Today, he wants yours.

lines.text: Fresher tax is not real. Repeat after me: fresher tax is not real.
Big Sly, if you're listening, Big Baby says come home. That's all.

scenes.title: Mission 8: Run am
scenes.context: Word of the court has gone round. Jega, the hall football captain, wants to see if the fresher who blocked Big Sly's boys can also ride.

lines.text: Theatre Loop tonight. If you hear screaming, it's either the race or Hassan.
Professor Shamsu missed an open goal. He blamed the wind. There was no wind.

scenes.title: Mission 9: Sly's last stand
scenes.context: Bolaji has heard about the race. He doesn't like freshers who are talked about more than he is.

lines.text: Big Sly has announced his retirement from tax. Freshers, walk freely. Walk proudly.
He's now a "consultant". Nobody knows what that means. Least of all Sly.

scenes.title: Mission 10: Stone that points
scenes.context: Light mission, a Saturday walk. Kelechi, the sculpture student a year ahead, says three of the statues point.

lines.text: Saturday! No lectures! Go and look at something you walk past every day.
A rock by the Dam is trending. Four likes. Lyzzy, please.

scenes.title: Mission 11: Baba Dam
scenes.context: The pier is rotten in three places. Baba Dam, the old fisherman, can't fix it alone.

lines.text: The pier at the Dam has been fixed by a fresher. Freshers fixing things. Wow.
Foreman Asabe says she mixed it. The fresher says they mixed it. Truth: cement.

scenes.title: Mission 12: Licence
scenes.context: Coach Danladi says real campus life is on three wheels. Get your keke licence by winning the Hostel Run — with two passengers in the back who will not stop talking.

lines.text: New keke drivers on the road today. Pedestrians: pray. Goats: pray harder.
Corporal Peter's wife's birthday is the fourteenth. Somebody buy the man a card.

scenes.title: Mission 13: Keke Grand Prix
scenes.context: The Ring Road Grand Prix: twelve kekes, one lap of the whole campus, a trophy made of an old exhaust pipe sprayed gold. Half the campus is watching.

lines.text: A wheel was seen leaving campus at speed. If found, return to number eleven.
The twins' video of the Grand Prix has more views than the Grand Prix.

scenes.title: Mission 14: The dam at midnight
scenes.context: Baba Dam's nets come up torn every night, and something under the water hums when the lights go out. He wants to see it.

lines.text: Lights at the Dam went out tonight. In order. Like a queue. Spooky.
Ranger Lawal says don't go to the Dam at night. He said it angrily.

scenes.title: Mission 15: The class of your life
scenes.context: Dr. Okonkwo takes the relay core, goes quiet, then gives you a choice: she'll explain what it is — after you score four out of five in her test.

lines.text: Kainji Theatre lost power mid-test. Dr. Okonkwo continued. Legend. Menace.
lines.scene: Mission 15: The class of your life

lines.text: Students wrote by phone light. It looked beautiful. It was not beautiful inside.
lines.scene: Mission 15: The class of your life

scenes.title: Mission 16: Gather the crew
scenes.context: The Maker says the shades will gather at the Senate on the night of the next blackout, and that one person with a torch is a snack. Five people with torches is a problem for them.

lines.text: A crew is forming. I don't know for what. I'm excited anyway.
KB has raised the price of batteries. When KB raises batteries, the night is coming.

scenes.title: Mission 17: Count Entropy
scenes.context: The blackout comes on Thursday, as the Maker said. The shades pour across the boulevard to the Senate.

lines.text: The lights are back! Campus is dancing! Malam Garba is dancing! History!
Did anyone else see a tall man on the Senate steps? No? Just me? Good.

scenes.title: Mission 18: Wings
scenes.context: Captain Uche has watched freshers dance at the Senate on her phone. She says anybody who can make a campus dance can learn to make a plane climb.

lines.text: A plane flew over the market this morning. A fresher. Waving. Possibly crying.
First semester is over. If you passed, dance. If you didn't, also dance.

scenes.title: Mission 19: Up NEPA party
scenes.context: The light has stayed on for a whole week. DJ Kabiru says that deserves noise, and he needs a crowd, a snack table and somebody brave enough to dance first.

lines.text: Seven days of light. If you hear a bang, it's the celebration, not the transformer.
Shout-out to John Carter. He says his name is Abbas. Noted. Ignored.

scenes.title: Mission 20: Profile picture
scenes.context: Lyzzy says your profile picture is "a crime against your face". She will fix it, if you pose at four gardens before the light goes.

lines.text: New profile pictures everywhere. The Selfie Garden queue is longer than registration.
Somebody keeps sending me a cape emoji. Stop it. It's not funny. It's a little funny.

scenes.title: Mission 21: Express delivery
scenes.context: Emeka the okada rider has sprained his wrist on the busiest morning of the month. Four deliveries, his bike, your backpack, and his phone ringing the whole time.

lines.text: Emeka's okada was seen with a stranger on it. Emeka, blink twice if you're okay.
Somebody delivered wood to a cliff. On campus. I don't know either.

scenes.title: Mission 22: Senate Sprint
scenes.context: The Senate Sprint is one lap of the Senate and back, the shortest race on campus and the dirtiest. Coach Danladi enters you.

lines.text: The Senate Sprint! Big Sly on a skateboard. I repeat. On a skateboard.
Coach Danladi says the fountain is not a shortcut. He says it every year.

scenes.title: Mission 23: The hum
scenes.context: The Maker says the ground has started humming. He wants you to listen with him, at night, when the campus is quiet enough to hear what is under it.

lines.text: Students near Engineering report humming. It's not me. I'm off air. Goodnight.
A girl with an umbrella says see you Wednesday. It's Wednesday. I'm scared.

scenes.title: Mission 24: Two papers, one day
scenes.context: Physics test at nine. Mathematics test at nine.

lines.text: Two papers, one day. Registry has blinked. I repeat, registry has blinked.
If you sat last year's maths paper, congratulations, you're a year ahead.

scenes.title: Mission 25: Paper trail
scenes.context: Mai Shayi has noticed a man in a good suit who visits the Bank after closing, every time the light goes. He would like to know why.

lines.text: I have a biscuit tin full of evidence. I'm not saying what of. Biscuits, maybe.
New story on the bookshop noticeboard. Somebody out there can write. Who are you?

scenes.title: Mission 26: East Side Drift
scenes.context: The East Side Drift is a car race round the tightest corners on campus. Kelechi lost it last year to a senior who "drove like a poem".

lines.text: First rain! Everybody run! Nobody run! Walk carefully and look cool!
Shamsu from Electrical asks students to stop calling him Sheikh Biru. Noted, Sheikh.

scenes.title: Mission 27: What the net caught
scenes.context: Something in the water at the Dam took Baba Dam's net and dragged it under. Tonight the net came back, and it is full of something that is not fish.

lines.text: The coil in the garden is off. If you have a candle, light it. If you have two, share.
Big Sly seen hugging a phone at the court. I said nothing. I saw nothing.

scenes.title: Mission 28: Wingman
scenes.context: Sadiq likes Joy, the radio intern. Sadiq has never said more than "Toh" to her.

lines.text: Somebody brought me shea butter. That's all. Back to Kabiru.
lines.tone: Radio (Joy): a rare turn on the mic

lines.text: The Love Garden lamps are off. Couples, please sit at a respectable distance. Two phones.

scenes.title: Mission 29: Night market
scenes.context: With the Maker gone four days and the market dark at night, a gang of older boys calling themselves "the levy" are going stall to stall, collecting a "light fee" for lamps that don't exist.

lines.text: Samaru Market had no light and no levy tonight. One of those is good news.
Jega headed a man. With a ball. I wasn't there. I'm still proud.

scenes.title: Mission 30: Signal from the sky
scenes.context: Captain Uche wants a dusk flight "for the joy of it", a loop over the campus at the golden hour. Bring a camera.

lines.text: The coil is back on! Engineering Garden lit! Somebody tell Asiya!
Where did he go? Nobody knows. He came back. That's all I need.

scenes.title: Mission 31: The second eel
scenes.context: The thing in the water that pulled Baba Dam's net is a mother eel, very old and very large. Since the Maker's absence, the shades have been gathering on her, and she is lashing at

lines.text: A giant eel took kilishi from a student. If you see her, be polite.
Bature has asked me to say he is "eel-certified". I don't know what that means.

scenes.title: Mission 32: Six plaques
scenes.context: The Maker has the dynamo. To use it he needs three more things: a perfect answer, copper winding and a spark gap.

lines.text: Six plaques under the coil. Six places. If you know a seventh, keep it to yourself.
An old man in a coat is giving out riddles. If he asks you one, say "Which?"

scenes.title: Mission 33: School Marathon
scenes.context: The School Marathon is the whole campus on foot. Coach Danladi's prize this year is a generator, donated by the traders.

lines.text: The marathon! Bolaji disqualified for a tray. Lula and Faty disqualified for love.
Did anyone see a boy in white handing out water at the far turn? Nobody? Okay.

scenes.title: Mission 34: Everybody
scenes.context: The Maker has a generator, a dynamo and a coil that hums. He says that on convocation night, when the seniors graduate and the whole campus lights up, the dark will come for the light.

lines.text: Tonight I'm on air till sunrise. Bring snacks. Bring friends. Bring candles.
KB is selling candles at cost price. I repeat. KB. Cost price. Check the sky.

scenes.title: Mission 35: Blackout protocol
scenes.context: Three nights before convocation, the whole grid fails. Sgt.

lines.text: Nine hours. Thank you, campus. Thank you, John Carter. Thank you, tea.
Three days to convocation. Seniors, iron your gowns. Freshers, iron something.

scenes.title: Mission 36: Convocation night
scenes.context: Convocation night. The seniors graduate; every light on campus goes on at once; and Count Entropy, fully grown on a year of the school's fear, stands on the Senate steps.

lines.text: Convocation night. The seniors graduated. The freshers lit a coil. Everybody danced.
Good morning. The lamps are still on. Nobody touch them. Let them have this.

scenes.title: Mission 37: Stalite
scenes.context: You come back from the break and somebody else's name is on your bed. Sort it out before dark, and find out what "stalite" means.

lines.text: Welcome back, stalites. Freshers, the tall orange building is the Senate.
New paint on the boulevard. Smells like ambition. And kerosene.

scenes.title: Mission 38: Grand opening
scenes.context: The market is now a mall. Hajiya Ladi's goods are at the gate, her new shop is upstairs, and the only escalator goes up.

lines.text: Fifteen shops, two floors, one escalator that only goes up.

scenes.title: Mission 39: New drip
scenes.context: Alhaji Needle will sew your first native. It will be ready Thursday.

lines.text: Needle & Thread. Measured twice. Ready Thursday.

scenes.title: Mission 41: The mall never blinks
scenes.context: The whole campus goes dark at once. Across the road the mall is glowing like a ship.

lines.text: If your bulb just died, you're locked in to the only station still talking.

scenes.title: Mission 42: Meter reader
scenes.context: Every evening, just before the campus goes dark, a Works van leaves the substation and drives to the mall. Follow it without being seen.

lines.text: Shout-out to the mall. How do you people do it? No, seriously. How?

scenes.title: Mission 43: Department week
scenes.context: Your first department week: a quiz against the department next door, a five-a-side, and a dinner with a dress code and a speech.

lines.text: May the best department win. And may the worst one at least bring food.

scenes.title: Mission 44: Iron Mama hums
scenes.context: The Maker has listened to the ground for a year. He sends you where he cannot go: under the mall, after closing, to see what is making the hum.

lines.text: Six were planned. Count what you can see.

scenes.title: Mission 45: Shuttle strike
scenes.context: The shuttle drivers have parked over unpaid allowances. Phase 2 is four kilometres away and full of stranded students.

lines.text: Phase 2, we are thinking of you. From here. Where it is near.

scenes.title: Mission 46: Sly goes straight
scenes.context: Bolaji is opening a barber's chair in the mall. His old court boys think that is the funniest thing they have heard.

lines.text: Caller says Big Sly is a barber now. Caller, are you well?

scenes.title: Mission 48: Flying lesson two
scenes.context: Captain Uche wants your turns tidier. You want a photograph of the mall roof.

lines.text: Harmattan is here. Vaseline has become currency.

scenes.title: Mission 49: Chief Megawatt
scenes.context: The mall's owner invites you up. He would like to sponsor your department.

lines.text: Samaru Market Mall. We never close our eyes.

scenes.title: Mission 50: Bolaji's board
scenes.context: A skate contest in the mall car park. Bolaji, all six feet of him, needs a spotter, somebody to film, and somebody to believe it.

lines.text: Trick of the week belongs to a very large man. Respect.

scenes.title: Mission 52: Phase 2 goes dark
scenes.context: While the feeder is argued over, Phase 2 has had no light for a week. Water, torches and charged phones go out in convoy on the long road at night.

lines.text: To the convoy on the long road: the whole station is riding with you.

scenes.title: Mission 53: The second coil
scenes.context: The Maker reads the second plaque aloud. The coil under the mall needs three parts.

lines.text: A machine that needs one keeper is not finished.

scenes.title: Mission 54: Love in the time of NEPA
scenes.context: A plan for the evening. Then no light, and no money either.

lines.text: To everyone sitting in the dark with someone tonight: you're fine.
lines.scene: Mission 54: Love in the time of NEPA

scenes.title: Mission 55: Unplug Iron Mama (Heist 1: the mall plant room)
scenes.context: Plan it like professionals, earn the key from Sgt. Bilkisu on a night shift, then go down to a generator that has grown teeth, with your friends at every door.

lines.text: The mall just blinked. I repeat: the mall blinked.
lines.scene: Mission 55: Unplug Iron Mama (Heist 1: the mall plant room)

scenes.title: Mission 56: Light for everybody
scenes.context: The feeder must be switched back at three corners of campus, ninety seconds apart. Then a panel in the Senate asks what you saw, and reads your own choices back to you.

lines.text: Steady light. I don't know what to do with my hands.

scenes.title: Mission 57: Sign-out, small
scenes.context: Second-semester exams in steady light. Then the final-years sign out in white shirts, and you hold the markers.

lines.text: To the graduating set: go well. To everyone else: see you after the break.

scenes.title: Mission 58: Three hundred
scenes.context: Third year. The notice board puts you in a project group of four: two serious, one asleep in Pepsi Garden, one not seen since Tuesday.

lines.text: Three hundred level. The year the handouts get thicker and the jokes get thinner.

scenes.title: Mission 59: Indefinite
scenes.context: A sheet of paper on the Senate door. A congress at Theatre CD.

lines.text: This is Fresh FM, broadcasting to… I can see four people from this window.

scenes.title: Mission 60: Those who stayed
scenes.context: Count who is left: a tea seller, a nurse, a porter, a man with a coil, and you. No allowance is coming.

lines.text: Day nine. I have played every track twice. Send requests. Send anything.

scenes.title: Mission 63: Empty halls
scenes.context: Something is sitting in Kainji Theatre. Row after row of it.

lines.text: If you are sitting alone right now: stand up. Open the door. That's the show.

scenes.title: Mission 64: The sit-down
scenes.context: Your roommate has not left the room in four days. Not ill.

lines.text: Somebody opened a window today. I felt it from here.

scenes.title: Mission 66: Old Campus
scenes.context: Walls with trees growing through them. A plaque with the same marks as Kelechi's statues.

lines.text: If you are waiting for someone else to switch it on: so are they.

scenes.title: Mission 68: Night nurse
scenes.context: The Sick Bay generator is on its last cup. Fetch four jerrycans, driving as if eggs were in the back.

lines.text: To the Sick Bay: I can see your light from the studio. Whoever did that, respect.

scenes.title: Mission 69: The Idle King
scenes.context: NELT is full of it. You cannot hit silence, so bring a football crowd, an open mic, three radios and a bell.

lines.text: We can hear you from here.

scenes.title: Mission 70: Called off
scenes.context: The strike is over. The buses come back all at once, and Kabiru has hidden a treasure hunt across campus to welcome everybody.

lines.text: They've called it off! Come back! Bring your bags! Bring my listeners!

scenes.title: Mission 71: Bolaji's choice
scenes.context: The mall wants Bolaji skating in its adverts full-time. He has a withdrawal form half filled in.

lines.text: Whatever he decides, he lands on his feet. He always has.

scenes.title: Mission 72: Workshop nights
scenes.context: Group Light Work's project: solar lamps for the dark road to Phase 2. Dr.

lines.text: Something is glowing in an engineering lab after hours. For once, on purpose.

scenes.title: Mission 73: Test run
scenes.context: The first lamp goes up at dusk on the darkest bend. It comes on.

lines.text: One lamp on the long road. One. It looks like a star that got lost.

scenes.title: Mission 74: Ranger Lawal's debt
scenes.context: A patrol has not come back. He has turned you round three times.

lines.text: Rain. Finally. The dust has been owing us.

scenes.title: Mission 75: The third coil wakes
scenes.context: Old Campus has no power. Your project lamps do.

lines.text: Three.

scenes.title: Mission 76: Heartbreak, or not
scenes.context: After months apart, somebody is not where they used to be. Listen first.

lines.text: A letter tonight from someone who said the true thing and survived.

scenes.title: Mission 77: Wedding at the quarters
scenes.context: Malam Garba's daughter is marrying. You need an outfit, a gift and a place in the dance line.

lines.text: A dedication from the Senate porter's lodge to the newest couple in Staff Quarters.

scenes.title: Mission 78: Lights on the long road
scenes.context: Demo day on the quad, exams in a hurry, and then the last lamp. At dusk the whole road to Phase 2 lights up, pole by pole, and everybody rides it.

lines.text: Forty lamps. Students built them. I am not crying. It's harmattan. In June.
lines.scene: Mission 78: Lights on the long road

scenes.title: Mission 79: IT letter
scenes.context: One letter, four stamps, three offices, two "come back tomorrow"s and a bank queue. Then a choice of where you train for six months.

lines.text: Four hundred level, your IT letters are ready. "Ready" is doing a lot of work there.

scenes.title: Mission 81: Lucky goes viral
scenes.context: Somebody filmed your dance at The Floor and put a beat under it. By lunch the whole school has seen it, and a brand wants your feet.

lines.text: Trending on campus: a certain somebody at The Floor. You know yourself.

scenes.title: Mission 82: The collab
scenes.context: Lucky wants three stunts for one video: a wheelie down the boulevard, a wave from the Senate steps, a keke full of goats. Then you go to buy socks and forty people want a picture.

lines.text: A reminder that goats are not content. They are colleagues.

scenes.title: Mission 83: Echo
scenes.context: Mai Shayi says you were rude to him last night. You were asleep last night.

lines.text: A reminder that not everything you watch on a phone happened the way it looks.

scenes.title: Mission 85: Payday
scenes.context: Your first real allowance: ₦60,000. Home needs some.

lines.text: MIB Store. Original. Made in Bugaje.

scenes.title: Mission 86: Hock Day (the time loop)
scenes.context: Your roommate's birthday at the buka and Lucky's rooftop party fall on the same day. Then the day starts again.

lines.text: Is it just me, or has this week had four Thursdays?

scenes.title: Mission 87: Night flight (Heist 3: the old control tower)
scenes.context: The old control tower has been locked since before Captain Uche. The fourth plaque is inside, the stairs are full of Echoes, and the beacon must be lined up from the air on three passes.

lines.text: Four.
lines.scene: Mission 87: Night flight (Heist 3: the old control tower)

scenes.title: Mission 88: Fashion show
scenes.context: Alhaji Needle's collection on a runway through the mall. He needs a model who can walk and turn.

lines.text: The mall has a runway tonight. The escalator is jealous.

scenes.title: Mission 89: Cancelled
scenes.context: A clip of "you" shoving a fresher. It is an Echo.

lines.text: I'm not going to comment on a video. I'm going to play a song. A long one.

scenes.title: Mission 91: The real clip
scenes.context: Somebody's phone caught the real thing and fell in the fountain. Chi-Tech can save it for three favours.

lines.text: New video. Watch to the end. Then watch your own mouth next time. I'm talking to me too.

scenes.title: Mission 92: Double booking
scenes.context: Two people were promised the same evening. If it was you, face it.

lines.text: Tonight's letter is from two people who discovered they had one thing in common.

scenes.title: Mission 93: Cook-off
scenes.context: The food court is half the price and the buka is half empty. She will not ask for help.

lines.text: She is stirring. He is plating. Somebody at the back has fainted from the smell.

scenes.title: Mission 94: Election day
scenes.context: Comrade Sadiya is running again and Yakubu is her manager. Posters, a debate card that says "second speaker", and a ballot box that turns out to be under the returning officer's chair.

lines.text: Election season. Posters are covering posters that are covering posters.

scenes.title: Mission 95: The eel's bargain
scenes.context: The fifth coil is in the spillway under the Dam wall. Baba Dam will row you.

lines.text: Five.

scenes.title: Mission 96: The Mirror
scenes.context: A copy of you as tall as the FSLG letters, made of every clip ever filmed of you. Hit it and it hits back.

lines.text: Nobody filmed the end. I think that was the end.

scenes.title: Mission 97: Log off
scenes.context: What do you do with being known? Then a logbook on a table and a panel in a row: the industrial-training defence.

lines.text: This is Joy. Not anonymous any more. Hello. Properly.

scenes.title: Mission 98: Sadiq's surprise
scenes.context: You owe your roommate an apology for most of this year. Before you can give it, the whole room shouts "surprise".

lines.text: Caller reports a surprise party on the second floor. Caller was not invited. Hurt.

scenes.title: Mission 100: Finalist
scenes.context: Mission one hundred. Freshers call you "senior" and step off the path.

lines.text: Finalists, your clearance forms will not sign themselves. I checked.

scenes.title: Mission 101: The Maker's notebook
scenes.context: Choose a supervisor for your final-year project. Then the Maker gives you the book he has never shown anyone, half of it in a shorthand only your class could read.

lines.text: Six were planned.

scenes.title: Mission 102: Fresher tax, reversed
scenes.context: A new boy at the court is taxing freshers. Big Sly would like a word with him.

lines.text: The court is free. It was always free. Some people forgot.

scenes.title: Mission 103: Sixth site (Heist 2: the Senate basement)
scenes.context: The sixth plaque says only "at the centre". One reference is in a room the library does not admit to having, four corners of campus have to be measured, and the centre turns out to be a room

lines.text: Somebody measured the campus with a stick today. Engineers. We let them live among us.
lines.scene: Mission 103: Sixth site (Heist 2: the Senate basement)

scenes.title: Mission 104: Megawatt's offer
scenes.context: The coil costs more than a keke. Raise it honestly, or let Chief Megawatt pay for all of it and put his name on the tower.

lines.text: Students are selling puff-puff for science. Buy two. One is for the coil. One is for you.

scenes.title: Mission 105: Parts from everywhere
scenes.context: Six people each have one thing the coil needs. Each asks one small thing in return.

lines.text: If an engineering student asks you for your pot lid this week, say yes. Don't ask.

scenes.title: Mission 106: Build week
scenes.context: Frame. Two thousand turns of copper.

lines.text: Fire service at the engineering workshop. Everybody is fine. Somebody's project is not.

scenes.title: Mission 108: Everybody, again
scenes.context: Ten departments, one section of coil each, wound together in one hall. Go round the quad and ask.

lines.text: If you were in Kainji tonight, you built something. Tell your children.

scenes.title: Mission 109: The Chancellor's shadow
scenes.context: A letter on every board: "Convocation is cancelled." No signature. The paper is cold.

lines.text: Time: twenty-two hundred. Weather: clear. Stay.

scenes.title: Mission 110: Dinner night
scenes.context: Final-year dinner. Who you walk in with, where you sit, and what award the class votes you.

lines.text: A dedication to the graduating class from every aunty who ever sold them rice.

scenes.title: Mission 111: Project defence
scenes.context: The last test. Then you, a rebuilt coil under a cloth, and a panel that has failed better students.

lines.text: To whoever just walked out of NELT for the last time: turn round. Look at it. Okay. Go.

scenes.title: Mission 112: The longest night
scenes.context: Every light on campus goes at once and does not come back: lamps, mall, the long road, all five coils. Hold your hostel till the torches arrive, then walk three hundred students out.

lines.text: If you can hear this, walk toward the engineering side. Bring whoever is next to you.

scenes.title: Mission 113: Three by road
scenes.context: The Garden, the Mall and Old Campus, relit in one run. Everyone you met in Year 1 holds the first.

lines.text: Three lights on my horizon. Battery at forty per cent. Keep going.

scenes.title: Mission 114: Three by air and water
scenes.context: One pass over the tower beacon in a sky with no lights below. The eel lighting the spillway.

lines.text: Five. Battery at eleven per cent. I'll stop talking and just leave the microphone open.
lines.scene: Mission 114: Three by air and water

scenes.title: Mission 116: The Maker's graduation
scenes.context: The ring needs one more thing closed: the first keeper has to let go of the first coil. He takes off the lab coat and walks out of the garden.

lines.text: A thing is finished when it no longer needs you.
lines.tone: Radio (Bugaje Beats): for the last time

scenes.title: Mission 117: Gown
scenes.context: A name on a board, a gown from the mall, and five photographs in five places with whoever mattered most there.

lines.text: Photographers have outnumbered students. If you see grass, someone is posing on it.

scenes.title: Mission 118: Convocation
scenes.context: The voices on the phone arrive in person. Show them round.

lines.text: From the Senate porter's lodge, with pride, to every name read today.

scenes.title: Mission 119: Sign-out
scenes.context: A white shirt and a box of markers. What each friend writes depends on five years of what you did.

lines.text: To the graduating set. Go well. I'm not crying. It's harmattan.

scenes.title: Side mission 33: Kabiru off air
scenes.context: The studio mic is dead and he must MC a wedding in person. He is terrified.

lines.text: (on air) To the friend who held my shaking hand: you're locked in. Forever.

scenes.title: Side mission 43: Sugar's accounts
scenes.context: She has an accounting test tomorrow and a full floor tonight. Run the decks for one set.

lines.text: Debit the bass. Credit the drums. Don't touch the red button. EVER.
…The crowd loves it. Okay. Okay! Do it again!
My accounting lecturer was on the floor. He gave me an A for "rhythm".
(on air) DJ Sugar passed accounting! On the one! Debit, credit, dance!

scenes.title: Side mission 49: Jega's socks
scenes.context: The lucky socks are missing an hour before the final. They are on a hostel line.

lines.text: (on air) Hall final! Jega scores! In clean socks! Science is confused!

scenes.title: Side mission 52: Emily's strawberries (II): market day
scenes.context: The farm needs one good market day. Get the strawberries into three shops and onto the radio.

lines.text: Fresh FM presents: strawberries. That's the advert. They're good. Buy.

lines.text: We have a visitor! Wave for the listeners!
lines.tone: DJ Kabiru: through the window, on air

lines.text: They can't see you. It's radio. But they feel the wave.
Seven days of light! Seven! My fridge is confused. It thinks it's abroad.
Party at Shinkafi tonight. Up NEPA. I need snacks and I need a first dancer.
Our fresher has opened the floor! The rest of you, shame!
No. No no no. Seven days. We had seven days!
Light by generator! Light by John Carter!
I can't read this on air. It's numbers. Nobody dances to numbers.
But I'll keep it. In the studio safe. It's a biscuit tin. It's very safe.
All night? On air? With my voice? …Yes. Obviously yes. I was born for this.
If you can hear me, you have batteries. Congratulations. Stay inside.
No. No no no. If the radio stops, people panic. People panic, people go out.
People go out, the dark gets them. Fix it. Somebody fix it.
We're back! Thanks to a man called…
…John Carter!
I talked for nine hours. My voice is gone. My heart is full. Is that a song?
The coil is lit! The first light! Up NEPA! Up everybody!
On the one! Who is that? Give them space!
Good morning, it's Thursday, and the weather is the weather.
Clue thirty-three is where the yam lady sits. You know the yam lady.
Look how small you were. Now look at you. Still small. But senior.
Final year. Final remix. Final— no, I'll play it again tomorrow.
One hundred out of one hundred. Somebody give this person garri.
Fresh F M, ninety-nine point one. Your school, your sound.
Amapiano Lounge. Log drums till morning.
Highlife Gold. The classics your daddy danced to.
Arewa Calm. Breathe.
Night Drive. Lights low, windows down.
Street Breaks. Hold tight.
Hostel Funk, eighty-eight. Room to room.
Dub Plate. Heavy, heavy bass.
Bugaje Beats. From the man who built this place.
Parade Ground. Left, right, left.
Eight bit buka. You found us.
This one is for anybody in a room alone. You're not. Turn it up.
I'm not crying. It's harmattan. In April. Turn it up!
Ten clues, ten places. First crew to the fountain eats on me. Terms apply.
On the one! Shoulders! Yes!
Buka versus food court. Live. I'll commentate. I've been practising on football.
Mama Nkechi wins! Food court, please accept your loss with pepper.
And a special award to the goat. He was the only honest candidate.
For the sculptor. Eight statues, one signature. Go well.
One hundred things only a finalist would know. First: where did the suya man go?
Turn. Turn. Turn. I have never been so bored and so moved. Turn.
I'm on battery. I'll keep talking as long as it lasts. Somebody stay with me.
We're back. The lights aren't, but the music is. Priorities.
New mural at Phase Two! It's a goat. Of course it's a goat.
The sun is coming up, every lamp is on, and I have nothing clever to say. Well done.
…and Bature. Yes, him. I'm as surprised as you are.
Final broadcast for this lot. Play it loud. Play it slow.
You're locked in. …Who is locked in? Is that a student? Fine. Go.
People will look at me. Radio people are not for looking at.
You're locked in! The couple is locked in! Forever! Station ident!
Good evening, Samaru Quarters! Hold your plates, here comes love!
On the one! …I have accounting at eight. Debit is on the left. I think.
(from a corner, with a textbook) On the one! …Debit, credit. On the one!
You are tuned to Samaru FM!
Request line is open.
No dead air on my watch.
Good morning, freshers. The tall orange building is the Senate. Wave at it.
Today's weather: harmattan. Tomorrow's weather: also harmattan. Moisturise.
First lecture? Sit in the middle. Front row gets questions. Back gets sleep.
KB says bread is ₦300 for happy people. Look sad, save fifty naira.
The fountain has claimed three cyclists this week. The fountain is winning.
Library hours: until Mrs. Shehu says shh. Which is any minute.
Light has been taken. We are on battery. My voice is on battery. Speak softly.
If you see shadows moving in your corridor, it's your roommate. Probably.
Shout-out to the two mechanics arguing by the workshop. We can hear you. Live.
It's Wednesday. If a girl with an umbrella says "see you Wednesday", believe her.
Sculpture Garden at night? Bring a torch and a friend who isn't afraid. Two friends.
Somebody put a cap on the goat statue again. The goat looks better. Leave it.
Fresher tax is not real. Repeat after me: fresher tax is not real.
Big Sly, if you're listening, Big Baby says come home. That's all.
Theatre Loop tonight. If you hear screaming, it's either the race or Hassan.
Professor Shamsu missed an open goal. He blamed the wind. There was no wind.
Big Sly has announced his retirement from tax. Freshers, walk freely. Walk proudly.
He's now a "consultant". Nobody knows what that means. Least of all Sly.
Saturday! No lectures! Go and look at something you walk past every day.
A rock by the Dam is trending. Four likes. Lyzzy, please.
The pier at the Dam has been fixed by a fresher. Freshers fixing things. Wow.
Foreman Asabe says she mixed it. The fresher says they mixed it. Truth: cement.
New keke drivers on the road today. Pedestrians: pray. Goats: pray harder.
Corporal Peter's wife's birthday is the fourteenth. Somebody buy the man a card.
A wheel was seen leaving campus at speed. If found, return to number eleven.
The twins' video of the Grand Prix has more views than the Grand Prix.
Lights at the Dam went out tonight. In order. Like a queue. Spooky.
Ranger Lawal says don't go to the Dam at night. He said it angrily.
Kainji Theatre lost power mid-test. Dr. Okonkwo continued. Legend. Menace.

lines.text: Students wrote by phone light. It looked beautiful. It was not beautiful inside.

lines.text: A crew is forming. I don't know for what. I'm excited anyway.
KB has raised the price of batteries. When KB raises batteries, the night is coming.
The lights are back! Campus is dancing! Malam Garba is dancing! History!
Did anyone else see a tall man on the Senate steps? No? Just me? Good.
A plane flew over the market this morning. A fresher. Waving. Possibly crying.
First semester is over. If you passed, dance. If you didn't, also dance.
Seven days of light. If you hear a bang, it's the celebration, not the transformer.
Shout-out to John Carter. He says his name is Abbas. Noted. Ignored.
New profile pictures everywhere. The Selfie Garden queue is longer than registration.
Somebody keeps sending me a cape emoji. Stop it. It's not funny. It's a little funny.
Emeka's okada was seen with a stranger on it. Emeka, blink twice if you're okay.
Somebody delivered wood to a cliff. On campus. I don't know either.
The Senate Sprint! Big Sly on a skateboard. I repeat. On a skateboard.
Coach Danladi says the fountain is not a shortcut. He says it every year.
Students near Engineering report humming. It's not me. I'm off air. Goodnight.
A girl with an umbrella says see you Wednesday. It's Wednesday. I'm scared.
Two papers, one day. Registry has blinked. I repeat, registry has blinked.
If you sat last year's maths paper, congratulations, you're a year ahead.
I have a biscuit tin full of evidence. I'm not saying what of. Biscuits, maybe.
New story on the bookshop noticeboard. Somebody out there can write. Who are you?
First rain! Everybody run! Nobody run! Walk carefully and look cool!
Shamsu from Electrical asks students to stop calling him Sheikh Biru. Noted, Sheikh.
The coil in the garden is off. If you have a candle, light it. If you have two, share.
Big Sly seen hugging a phone at the court. I said nothing. I saw nothing.
Somebody brought me shea butter. That's all. Back to Kabiru.
lines.tone: Radio (Joy): a rare turn on the mic

lines.text: The Love Garden lamps are off. Couples, please sit at a respectable distance. Two phones.
Samaru Market had no light and no levy tonight. One of those is good news.
Jega headed a man. With a ball. I wasn't there. I'm still proud.
The coil is back on! Engineering Garden lit! Somebody tell Asiya!
Where did he go? Nobody knows. He came back. That's all I need.
A giant eel took kilishi from a student. If you see her, be polite.
Bature has asked me to say he is "eel-certified". I don't know what that means.
Six plaques under the coil. Six places. If you know a seventh, keep it to yourself.
An old man in a coat is giving out riddles. If he asks you one, say "Which?"
The marathon! Bolaji disqualified for a tray. Lula and Faty disqualified for love.
Did anyone see a boy in white handing out water at the far turn? Nobody? Okay.
Tonight I'm on air till sunrise. Bring snacks. Bring friends. Bring candles.
KB is selling candles at cost price. I repeat. KB. Cost price. Check the sky.
Nine hours. Thank you, campus. Thank you, John Carter. Thank you, tea.
Three days to convocation. Seniors, iron your gowns. Freshers, iron something.
Convocation night. The seniors graduated. The freshers lit a coil. Everybody danced.
Good morning. The lamps are still on. Nobody touch them. Let them have this.
Welcome back, stalites. Freshers, the tall orange building is the Senate.
New paint on the boulevard. Smells like ambition. And kerosene.
Fifteen shops, two floors, one escalator that only goes up.
Needle & Thread. Measured twice. Ready Thursday.
If your bulb just died, you're locked in to the only station still talking.
Shout-out to the mall. How do you people do it? No, seriously. How?
May the best department win. And may the worst one at least bring food.
Six were planned. Count what you can see.
Phase 2, we are thinking of you. From here. Where it is near.
Caller says Big Sly is a barber now. Caller, are you well?
Harmattan is here. Vaseline has become currency.
Samaru Market Mall. We never close our eyes.
Trick of the week belongs to a very large man. Respect.
To the convoy on the long road: the whole station is riding with you.
A machine that needs one keeper is not finished.
To everyone sitting in the dark with someone tonight: you're fine.

lines.text: Steady light. I don't know what to do with my hands.

Three hundred level. The year the handouts get thicker and the jokes get thinner.
This is Fresh FM, broadcasting to… I can see four people from this window.
Day nine. I have played every track twice. Send requests. Send anything.
If you are sitting alone right now: stand up. Open the door. That's the show.
Somebody opened a window today. I felt it from here.

We can hear you from here.
They've called it off! Come back! Bring your bags! Bring my listeners!
Whatever he decides, he lands on his feet. He always has.
Something is glowing in an engineering lab after hours. For once, on purpose.
One lamp on the long road. One. It looks like a star that got lost.
Rain. Finally. The dust has been owing us.
Three.
A letter tonight from someone who said the true thing and survived.
A dedication from the Senate porter's lodge to the newest couple in Staff Quarters.
Forty lamps. Students built them. I am not crying. It's harmattan. In June.

Trending on campus: a certain somebody at The Floor. You know yourself.
A reminder that goats are not content. They are colleagues.
A reminder that not everything you watch on a phone happened the way it looks.
MIB Store. Original. Made in Bugaje.
Is it just me, or has this week had four Thursdays?
Four.

Five.
