lines.text: Where did you get that machine? …Where did you get that tape?
I was the sixth stool.
My project was the ring. You cannot submit one sixth of a project. So I stayed.
I thought if I left, the light would go. I may have been right. I never tested it.

scenes.title: Mission 69: The Idle King
scenes.context: NELT is full of it. You cannot hit silence, so bring a football crowd, an open mic, three radios and a bell.

lines.text: The largest hall holds the largest quiet. Fill it. With anything.

scenes.title: Mission 70: Called off
scenes.context: The strike is over. The buses come back all at once, and Kabiru has hidden a treasure hunt across campus to welcome everybody.

lines.text: I was told to hand this over only to someone noisy.

scenes.title: Mission 75: The third coil wakes
scenes.context: Old Campus has no power. Your project lamps do.

lines.text: I made this the year I should have graduated. It fits. I never got to see it fit.

scenes.title: Mission 77: Wedding at the quarters
scenes.context: Malam Garba's daughter is marrying. You need an outfit, a gift and a place in the dance line.

lines.text: I can hear three coils. I thought I could spare an hour.
A poet wrote: "He who abides far away from his home
Is ever longing for the day he shall return." I'm only visiting. Dance.

scenes.title: Mission 96: The Mirror
scenes.context: A copy of you as tall as the FSLG letters, made of every clip ever filmed of you. Hit it and it hits back.

lines.text: It is made of how you look. It has never seen what you are for. Show it.

scenes.title: Mission 105: Parts from everywhere
scenes.context: Six people each have one thing the coil needs. Each asks one small thing in return.

lines.text: You can't buy these. You can only be given them.

scenes.title: Mission 116: The Maker's graduation
scenes.context: The ring needs one more thing closed: the first keeper has to let go of the first coil. He takes off the lab coat and walks out of the garden.

lines.text: It won't close while I'm holding the first one. I understand it now. It's arithmetic.
Come and walk with me. I've forgotten the way to the Senate.
I kept this for a long time. Thank you. I don't need it.

scenes.title: Mission 118: Convocation
scenes.context: The voices on the phone arrive in person. Show them round.

lines.text: I recommend about five years. I took the scenic route.

scenes.title: The Maker's sayings
scenes.context: After the ring is lit, the Maker walks the campus free. Talking to him gives one saying. Dry, kind and exact; a smile you can hear.

lines.text: Energy in, light out. The rest is commentary.
A thing is finished when it no longer needs you.
I kept one light on for a long time. You taught me to share the switch.
Nobody lights a ring alone. I checked. For years.
The dark is not an enemy. It is what is there before somebody bothers.
Start small. A torch has never been embarrassed by the sun.
If you are tired, rest. If you are stuck, move. Learn which one it is.
The best machine I ever built was a queue of people passing parts.
Read the manual. Then read the person.
You will forget the grade. You will remember who lent you a pen.
Every expert was once the one asking where the Senate is.
Measure twice. Then ask someone to measure. Then cut.
A carry-over is a second lecture you paid for with pride.
Money is stored effort. Spend it on what stores well: skills, friends, shoes.
The loudest person in the room is usually running on low battery.
Be the reason the fresher finds the hall.
I used to think staying was loyalty. Sometimes leaving is how you keep faith.
Light travels fast. Kindness travels further.
When they take light, sit near people. That is the whole trick.
Entropy always wins in the end. So enjoy the middle and tidy as you go.
A good question is worth two answers and one cup of tea.
Do not confuse being seen with being known.
The coil hums at one note. Find yours. It need not be loud.
Borrow tools. Return them cleaner. This is most of ethics.
Your friends are your backup generator. Service them regularly.
The shortest path is rarely the one with the best suya.
I have watched forty first days. Every one of them looked like fear and was actually hope.
Garri week comes to us all. Share the cup.
A lecture is someone handing you ten years in fifty minutes. Sit up.
Whatever you practise at night is who you are by morning.
Fame is a lamp pointed at you. Useful is a lamp you hold.
Greet the porter. He was here before you and will be here after.
You cannot solder in a hurry. The same is true of trust.
If the plan needs a hero, it is a bad plan. Draw it again with a team.
The school is not the buildings. I learned this late. Learn it early.
It is allowed to be proud of something small.
Call home. They do not need news. They need your voice.
The exam ends. The understanding is yours to keep.
When you leave, leave something switched on.
I was a student here for longer than was sensible. I recommend about five years.
Stand where the fresher can see you. That is what seniors are for.
Some days the bravest thing is to open the door and go to class.
A switch has two positions. People have more. Be patient with them.
Thank you. I do not say it enough, and I had a lot of time to practise.

scenes.title: Mission 44: Iron Mama hums
scenes.context: The Maker has listened to the ground for a year. He sends you where he cannot go: under the mall, after closing, to see what is making the hum.

lines.text: A thermodynamically incontinent leviathan, hoarding our electrons.
A greedy generator.
She built the second one under the market. They built a mall on her.
Good. Now we know where. We do not yet know who.
I walked. A long way round a short problem. It is how old men think.
No. It is a direction.
Some things are drawn by people who wait for other people. Drink your tea.

scenes.title: Mission 48: Flying lesson two
scenes.context: Captain Uche wants your turns tidier. You want a photograph of the mall roof.

lines.text: You flew low over the fish pond. Thank you. Some things like to be seen.

scenes.title: Mission 53: The second coil
scenes.context: The Maker reads the second plaque aloud. The coil under the mall needs three parts.

lines.text: Energy in, light out. Now we need a key, and a night.
And a plan. Your friend with the riddles. Bring him. He is useful.
One lit. The second sleeps under a shopping bag. Absurd. Magnificent. Absurd.
My niece cooks like my mother. Do not tell her. She will become insufferable.
You. On a good day.

scenes.title: Mission 55: Unplug Iron Mama (Heist 1: the mall plant room)
scenes.context: Plan it like professionals, earn the key from Sgt. Bilkisu on a night shift, then go down to a generator that has grown teeth, with your friends at every door.

lines.text: Antidisestablishmentarian it is not. But it was splendiferous.
lines.scene: Mission 55: Unplug Iron Mama (Heist 1: the mall plant room)

lines.text: Two of them were. It went well.
lines.scene: Mission 55: Unplug Iron Mama (Heist 1: the mall plant room)

scenes.title: Mission 56: Light for everybody
scenes.context: The feeder must be switched back at three corners of campus, ninety seconds apart. Then a panel in the Senate asks what you saw, and reads your own choices back to you.

lines.text: Steady light. It is not glamorous. It is better than glamorous.
Ordinary, every night, for everyone. Go to bed.

scenes.title: Mission 57: Sign-out, small
scenes.context: Second-semester exams in steady light. Then the final-years sign out in white shirts, and you hold the markers.

lines.text: Two lit. Four dark. A good year.
Stand somewhere good next year. Ground remembers who stood on it.
I may be away a while again. If the lights go, do not panic. Then panic a little.

scenes.title: Mission 60: Those who stayed
scenes.context: Count who is left: a tea seller, a nurse, a porter, a man with a coil, and you. No allowance is coming.

lines.text: An empty school runs down faster. Come by. I like the noise you make.

scenes.title: Mission 63: Empty halls
scenes.context: Something is sitting in Kainji Theatre. Row after row of it.

lines.text: You cannot hit silence. You can only outnumber it. We need the people back.
Empty rooms remember people. That is why they are dangerous. Take a radio. Two.

scenes.title: Mission 67: The Maker's secret
scenes.context: You play him the last tape. He hears his own name, and for the first time since you met him, he sits down.

lines.text: Good question. I have had a long time and I still do not know. Ask me in two years.
A poet wrote, long ago: "Hearken to the reed-flute, how it discourses
When complaining of the pains of separation." I used to think it was about flutes.
I have been perambulating the perimeter of my own procrastination.
Thirty years. Yes.
I knew you would come tonight. The coil told me. It hums higher when you're near.
Professor, I'll stay. Just until they come back. A semester. Maybe two.
Five went home. One became a minister. One became nobody. One married.
And two I don't know. I didn't ask. Asking would have meant I'd stopped waiting.
Some names I keep in a pocket. If I take them out, they get cold.
She was always better at feeding fish than I was. Ask me in two years.
Someone who loves you more than they trust you. It's common. Forgive it early.
Your friend. The one with the riddles. He sat with me without a joke.
That is the bravest thing a funny man can do. Tell him I said so.

scenes.title: Mission 68: Night nurse
scenes.context: The Sick Bay generator is on its last cup. Fetch four jerrycans, driving as if eggs were in the back.

lines.text: The Sick Bay was dark for one night less than it would have been. Good.
The coil hums higher when a building is cared for. Sleep now.

scenes.title: Mission 70: Called off
scenes.context: The strike is over. The buses come back all at once, and Kabiru has hidden a treasure hunt across campus to welcome everybody.

lines.text: I know. I wanted to see what the inside thought of the world. Here. Clue ten.

scenes.title: Mission 75: The third coil wakes
scenes.context: Old Campus has no power. Your project lamps do.

lines.text: Three. I can hear three. …Thank you. I don't say it enough.
Triskaidekaphobia I have none; trinities I adore. Three!
I am just happy.
It was always mine. My niece keeps it so I have to visit her. Clever girl.

scenes.title: Mission 78: Lights on the long road
scenes.context: Demo day on the quad, exams in a hurry, and then the last lamp. At dusk the whole road to Phase 2 lights up, pole by pole, and everybody rides it.

lines.text: Three lit. Three dark. One is in the sky. One is under water.
lines.scene: Mission 78: Lights on the long road

lines.text: And one has never been built. But that is a final-year problem.
lines.scene: Mission 78: Lights on the long road

scenes.title: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden
scenes.context: Each plaque is read aloud when the player stands at it. Read like a guide in a museum, slowly. These are long: one breath per sentence is fine, but keep every pause under half a second.

lines.text: The coil above you is his: a resonant transformer he built in 1891 that turns ordinary voltage into hundreds of thousands of volts and throws it into the air as sparks. Tesla designed the AC induction motor and the polyphase system that still carries power across whole countries. The unit of magnetic flux density, the tesla, carries his name.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: A bookbinder's apprentice with almost no schooling. In 1831 he showed that a changing magnetic field drives a current: electromagnetic induction. Every generator and every transformer on this campus works because of that one experiment. The farad, the unit of capacitance, is named after him.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: He wrote the equations that tie electricity, magnetism and light together, and predicted that light itself is an electromagnetic wave. Radio, radar, Wi-Fi and the phone in your pocket all follow from those equations.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: A schoolteacher who measured, patiently, how current depends on voltage and resistance, and published V = IR in 1827. His own colleagues dismissed it at first. It is now the first line of every circuits course, including yours.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: Within weeks of hearing that a current deflects a compass, he worked out the force between two current-carrying wires and founded electrodynamics. The ampere, the unit of current, honours him.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: The engineer behind everything you are standing in. M.I. BUGAJE built EE Hub, the department's whole online home, and then built Freshers School Life on top of it: this campus, these roads, the classes, the okadas, the shades and the story. The scientists on the other plaques explained how the world works. He used it to build a world. If you are enjoying the game, find him and say thank you.

lines.text: The coil above you is his: a resonant transformer he built in 1891 that turns ordinary voltage into hundreds of thousands of volts and throws it into the air as sparks. Tesla designed the AC induction motor and the polyphase system that still carries power across whole countries. The unit of magnetic flux density, the tesla, carries his name.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: A bookbinder's apprentice with almost no schooling. In 1831 he showed that a changing magnetic field drives a current: electromagnetic induction. Every generator and every transformer on this campus works because of that one experiment. The farad, the unit of capacitance, is named after him.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: He wrote the equations that tie electricity, magnetism and light together, and predicted that light itself is an electromagnetic wave. Radio, radar, Wi-Fi and the phone in your pocket all follow from those equations.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: A schoolteacher who measured, patiently, how current depends on voltage and resistance, and published V = IR in 1827. His own colleagues dismissed it at first. It is now the first line of every circuits course, including yours.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: Within weeks of hearing that a current deflects a compass, he worked out the force between two current-carrying wires and founded electrodynamics. The ampere, the unit of current, honours him.
lines.scene: The six plaques in the Engineering Garden

lines.text: The engineer behind everything you are standing in. M.I. BUGAJE built EE Hub, the department's whole online home, and then built Freshers School Life on top of it: this campus, these roads, the classes, the okadas, the shades and the story. The scientists on the other plaques explained how the world works. He used it to build a world. If you are enjoying the game, find him and say thank you.

lines.text: The coil above you is his: a resonant transformer he built in 1891 that turns ordinary voltage into hundreds of thousands of volts and throws it into the air as sparks. lines.text: A bookbinder's apprentice with almost no schooling. In 1831 he showed that a changing magnetic field drives a current: electromagnetic induction. lines.text: He wrote the equations that tie electricity, magnetism and light together, and predicted that light itself is an electromagnetic wave. Radio, radar, Wi-Fi and the phone in your pocket all follow from those equations.
